# Model 6 (Feature Selection)

It now feels like time to focus in on suspected high impact variables, including annual_income, avg_transaction_value, num_transactions, and credit_score. I also again included the invented income_interaction variable.

```{python}
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')
features = ['annual_income', 'avg_transaction_value', 'num_transactions', 
                     'credit_score']
X = data[features].fillna(data[features].median())
X['income_interaction'] = X['num_transactions'] * X['avg_transaction_value']
y = data.monthly_spend

reg = LinearRegression()
reg.fit(X,y)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')
scoring_X = scoring_data[features].fillna(data[features].median())
scoring_X['income_interaction'] = scoring_X['num_transactions'] * scoring_X['avg_transaction_value']
pred = reg.predict(scoring_X)

submission_file = pd.DataFrame({'customer_id': scoring_data.customer_id, 'monthly_spend': pred})
submission_file.to_csv('../PACFiles/submission_file_7.csv', index=False)

from sklearn.metrics import root_mean_squared_error
train_pred = reg.predict(X)
rmse = root_mean_squared_error(y, train_pred)
print("Training RMSE:", rmse)
```
